Test whether two graphs are Markov equivalent

Source: R/identification.R
markov_equivalent.Rd

Returns TRUE if g1 and g2 (both DAGs, or both MAGs) belong to the same Markov equivalence class, i.e. they impose the same (conditional-)independence constraints.

Usage

markov_equivalent(g1, g2)

Arguments

g1, g2

Graphs to compare, created with cgraph(). Both must be DAGs, or both must be MAGs.

Value

A logical scalar.

Details

For DAGs, this holds iff they share the same skeleton and the same set of v-structures (unshielded colliders a --> b <-- c with a, c non-adjacent) - the Verma-Pearl characterization. For MAGs, this holds iff they map to the same PAG.

References

Verma T, Pearl J (1990). “Equivalence and synthesis of causal models.” In Proceedings of UAI 1990.

Ali RA, Richardson TS, Spirtes P (2009). “Markov equivalence for ancestral graphs.” Annals of Statistics, 37(5B), 2808–2837.

Examples

if (julia_ready()) {
  g1 <- cgraph(A %-->% B, C %-->% B)
  g2 <- cgraph(A %-->% B, C %-->% B)
  g3 <- cgraph(A %-->% B, B %-->% C)
  list(
    same_skeleton_same_v_structures = markov_equivalent(g1, g2),
    different_v_structures = markov_equivalent(g1, g3)
  )
}
#> $same_skeleton_same_v_structures
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $different_v_structures
#> [1] FALSE
#>
